narrative.summary: Comoros has no AI-specific law, strategy or guidance. Its only AI-relevant national instrument is the 2014 personal data protection law, which covers automated processing and creates a national data protection commission but has no rule on automated individual decisions. AI is discussed only at forums under the digital economy ministry, and the official text of the Comores Numérique 2028 digital strategy was not found. Several government websites could not be accessed during this review.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026, but the digital agency, digital ministry and government portal websites could not be accessed and the official gazette has no online search, so only one document could be read. Comoros is marked for a later retry.

instruments.current_status: The text published on the Ministry of Justice legislation portal (listed as 'Loi du 26 juin 2014 portant protection des données à caractère personnel') is the version deliberated and adopted in plenary by the Assembly of the Union on 26 June 2014; its law number is left blank ('Loi N°14-_____/AU') and no promulgation decree or gazette reference was found on official sites, so the date recorded is the adoption date and the entry-into-force date is unknown. The law contains no AI-specific provisions and no rule on automated individual decisions; it is recorded because it governs automated processing of personal data.
instruments.summary: Comoros' personal data protection law, applying to automated and manual processing of personal data, including national identification mechanisms based on biometric data and unique identification numbers. It sets processing principles and data-subject rights, requires prior formalities with the regulator for automated processing, and creates the Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés (CNIL), an independent administrative body of nine members that oversees compliance. Article 2 states that computing must not harm human identity, privacy, human rights or public and individual liberties.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only general law found that governs automated processing of personal data used in AI systems; no AI-specific provisions.
